To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HES1 is expressed in biliary epithelum and prevents the pancreatic differentiation program by repressing transcriptional activation of NEUROG3.
the Notch/Hes1 pathway determines the fate of the extrahepatically located biliary epithelum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control the development of the pancreas and the biliary system.
the development of the pancreas and biliary tree and the mechanisms that control the development and maintenance of their cell lineages.
the role of the Notch pathway in development and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hes1 determines organogenesis of the biliary tract by preventing pancreatic differentiation.
Hes1 represses the expression of neurog3, which in turn prevents the conversion of biliary tissue to pancreas.
the biliary epithelum has the potential to develop into pancreatic tissue, but this potential is suppressed by Hes1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the biliary epithelum has a potential to differentiate into pancreatic endocrine and exocrin cells, and that Hes-1 is the factor that determines biliary organogensesis by preventing the pancreatic program of differentiation, possibly by direct repression of Neurog-3.
the biliary epithelum has the potential for pancreas development.
Hes1 acts as a master regulator for biliary organogenesis and that Hes family genes are important in organ development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biliary epithelum is not just a simple epithelium.

the Notch signaling pathway is a critical regulator of organogenesis in the developing gut.
